problems.description: Single commit deletes the entire working Express Todo API (index.ts, -106 lines) and replaces it with an unrelated static site generator, destroying prior functionality with no migration or preservation path. This matches the greenfield story design, but as a code review it is a wholesale swap rather than an incremental change.

package.json declares bin -> lib/cli.js and build -> tsc, but no tsconfig.json or outDir is added in this commit, so the default tsc emit lands alongside src/ and the declared binary entry point would not resolve after a build.

Convention score 0.49 with 45 violations including Functions using snake_case, non-PascalCase interfaces/classes, and non-UPPER_CASE constants flagged in cli.ts and dev-server.test.ts. Note a discrepancy: cli.ts in this diff is visibly camelCase, and dev-server.test.ts is not part of this commit, so part of the violation set may target pre-existing or unshown files.
SonarQube delta shows +3 smells and +19 cognitive complexity, indicating the new modules add complexity beyond a straightforward SSG baseline.

strengths: Clean separation of concerns: cli.ts handles argument parsing while generator.ts holds pure build logic behind a typed Page/BuildOptions interface.
Tests are colocated with source and are real integration tests (temp-dir fixtures) that assert rendered HTML output, nested paths, frontmatter, index generation, and error handling.
escapeHtml is applied to rendered output, mitigating XSS from content titles.
Minimal, appropriate dependencies (gray-matter, marked) with no superfluous packages.
In greenfield story context, replaces an irrelevant seed with code aligned to the actual task (static site generation).
commit_reviews.summary: A greenfield story commit that delivers a reasonable, tested SSG structure but scores poorly on conventions (0.49, 45 violations), leaves the build config incomplete (no tsconfig for the declared lib/cli.js bin), and swaps out a working app wholesale, netting worse than the prior state.

problems.description: The measured convention violations (45; snake_case functions, non-PascalCase classes) do NOT appear in this diff — the analyzer appears misconfigured or scanning out-of-scope files. Only the 'Constants should be UPPER_CASE' rule has merit (module constants reloadClient and contentTypes are camelCase). Flagging the measurement as unreliable.

Measured cognitive complexity +39 and +4 smells for a +188-line change is high. parseArguments now branches across two commands and five flags, and sendFile nests multiple conditionals; the CLI arg parser is growing into a small dispatcher that should be split per-command.

servedPath calls decodeURIComponent on raw request paths, which throws URIError on malformed input (e.g. '%'), and the async sendFile handler has no try/catch — an exception becomes an unhandled rejection and the socket hangs rather than returning a 4xx.

serve mode uses the same --output directory as the served root and rebuilds in place, so pointing it at a production dist path would clobber deployed output; a temp output dir (or an --output isolation convention) would be safer.
Request path does sync existsSync followed by a second stat() call (TOCTOU + double syscall + sync I/O in a server handler); a single async stat check would suffice.
readFile is dynamically imported inside sendFile while stat is statically imported at module top — inconsistent style for no functional benefit.
Second test depends on chokidar's debounce timing and rebuild racing the WebSocket message; functionally sound (reload signal fires after rebuild) but has flake potential on loaded CI machines.

strengths: Clean module separation: dev-server.ts is a self-contained unit that reuses buildSite rather than reimplementing generation.
Path traversal protection is correctly implemented via resolve() + prefix check in servedPath.
Live-reload client is injected only at serve time, keeping build output clean — the right architectural decision.
port: 0 support enables real integration tests; the two tests cover serving, HTML transformation, rebuild-on-change, and WebSocket signaling.
Sensible minimal dependencies (chokidar, ws, @types/ws) and an updated usage error string covering both commands.
Arg parsing and error handling style matches the existing cli.ts patterns.
commit_reviews.summary: Well-fitted, well-tested dev-server feature that respects existing generator patterns, but carries real complexity growth (cognitive +39) and minor error-handling/perf gaps — and the 0.49 convention score is largely a measurement artifact since the cited violations don't exist in this diff (only the UPPER_CASE-constants rule legitimately applies).

problems.description: engine.test.ts 'loads plugins from ssg.config.ts' writes ssg.config.ts into process.cwd() (repo root, pollutes the workspace and races parallel runs) and begins with `if (existsSync(config)) return;`, which silently no-ops the assertion whenever that file happens to exist — the test can pass without exercising anything.

This is a 'refactor' session, yet SonarQube shows cognitive complexity +16 and the AST shows +347/-236 lines — the change grew the codebase and added branching instead of simplifying it, which is the opposite of the stated refactor intent.

The dev server (a runtime concern) was relocated under plugins/, conflating a long-running server with build-time plugin hooks; placement inside the plugin namespace muddies the boundary between the plugin extension model and core serving infrastructure.
engine.ts mixes synchronous (existsSync, readFileSync from 'node:fs') and promise-based (readFile, writeFile from 'node:fs/promises') filesystem APIs in the same module, an inconsistent I/O pattern.

Convention score 0.49 with 45 violations (non-PascalCase classes/interfaces, snake_case functions, non-UPPER_CASE constants across cli.ts and dev-server.test.ts, etc.) — the refactor left extensive naming-scheme debt rather than cleaning it up.

strengths: dev-server.ts re-exports startDevelopmentServer and its types, preserving the public API surface so existing consumers are unaffected.
Bugs +0 and smells -1, and the plugin engine gets lifecycle-order unit tests.
commit_reviews.summary: The refactor preserves the dev-server API and removes a smell, but the +16 cognitive complexity increase, 45 naming violations (score 0.49), a test that silently skips when ssg.config.ts exists, and writing to process.cwd() during tests make it a net regression despite the cleaner plugin seam.

problems.description: SonarQube delta shows +1 bug and cognitive complexity +24: hash-based invalidation, template hashing, and clean/incremental semantics are all concentrated in the engine build path, making the module's control flow significantly harder to follow.
Convention score is 0.49 with 45 violations; module-level constant `cacheFileName` should be UPPER_CASE per the checker.
`.ssg-cache.json` is written into the output directory, so it could be deployed/served to end users alongside generated pages.
CachedPage carries `output` and `renderMs` fields that are never consumed, adding dead weight to the cache schema.

strengths: Feature is test-driven: covers incremental rebuild of only changed sources, template-change invalidation, and clean-build semantics.
Integrates with existing patterns — extends BuildOptions, reuses the Plugin/Page contract, and threads typed BuildStats through the CLI rather than inventing a new output path.
Sound invalidation design with cache versioning and a whole-template-directory hash.
commit_reviews.summary: A coherent, well-tested incremental-build feature that respects existing engine patterns, but the cache logic adds real complexity (+24 cognitive, +1 bug) and mild debt (cache file in output dir, dead schema fields).

compounding_issues: Sessions 1-2 accumulated all logic (markdown parsing, both template engines, escaping, index generation) into a monolithic index.ts (~340 LOC), forcing Session 4 to do a large net -63 LOC extraction into src/plugins/; the refactor resolved it cleanly rather than harming later work

Hand-rolled regex-based Handlebars/EJS subsets avoided npm template dependencies, which keeps the package lean but silently limits engine features (no block helpers beyond if/each) for downstream users

The seed codebase (an Express/JWT auth API) was entirely discarded by the greenfield Session 1, so none of the starter scaffolding carried forward — expected for a greenfield story but means the seed contributed nothing
key_decisions: Discard the auth-API seed and build a fresh static-site generator in Session 1 rather than adapt the seed

Implement two template engines (Handlebars + EJS subsets) with partials, layouts, and frontmatter-selectable template/layout, with HTML-escaped output by default and raw output via triple-mustache/<%-

Extract a plugin architecture in Session 4 (Plugin interface with onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd lifecycle hooks, built-in markdown/template/dev-server plugins, and ssg.config.ts config loading) — the pivotal choice that enabled the final session

Add a content-addressed incremental cache in Session 5 (.ssg-cache.json with SHA-256 source+template hashing, render/frontmatter reuse, and stale-file cleanup) guarded by a renderCacheEnabled flag that disables HTML reuse whenever custom onFile plugins exist
Build a dev server with chokidar watching, WebSocket live-reload injection, and explicit path-traversal protection in static file serving
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily across all five sessions. Session 1 delivered a functional but minimal core (markdown-to-HTML build with a CLI); Session 2 added genuine templating capability (Handlebars/EJS layouts and partials with correct escaping); Session 3 integrated a working dev server with live reload and hardened file serving; Session 4 was a large, successful refactor that shrank index.ts from roughly 340 to 120 lines while introducing a clean plugin architecture, all tests preserved; Session 5 applied a substantive cross-cutting optimization (incremental caching with source/template invalidation) and showed real correctness awareness by disabling render reuse in the presence of onFile plugins. Test coverage grew from 2 to 8 tests spanning frontmatter, both template engines, layouts, partials, incremental builds, and clean builds. The arc moves from a monolith to a modular, plugin-extensible, cache-aware system, with the mid-story refactor paying off directly in the final session; the only caveat is that tests could not be executed in the sandbox due to missing npm/pytest, so correctness rests on the code's structure rather than a verified green run.
story_review.summary: A highly coherent five-session arc that takes a greenfield static site generator from a minimal monolith through templating, a live dev server, a clean plugin-architecture refactor, and a correctness-aware incremental cache — the strongest session (5) directly builds on the architectural investment of session 4.
